title: Ada and the Bakery
premise: Ada Lindqvist built Salt & Crumb, the island's beloved bakery, out of the ashes of a failed city career, guarding her anonymity like flour dusted over old scars. When a November snowstorm traps her overnight in Sandoval Books with Emrys Sandoval—the guarded single father who has quietly loved her from across the street for two years—and with Theo Marchetti, the developer whose waterfront project would raze her bakery and whose history with Ada goes back to the best mistake of their twenties, every buried truth surfaces. As Theo's corruption of the town council accelerates and Ada's old mentor offers her a career-saving post in Copenhagen, she must decide whether belonging is something you inherit or something you build. On the day of the last ferry of the season, Ada chooses the island, the bakery, and Emrys—turning the council vote by exposing Theo's forged permits and finally letting herself be seen.
about_author: Odile Crane is the pen name of a former line cook who traded professional kitchens for small-town romances set against cold water and warm ovens. She writes from a coastal cottage where the ferry schedule dictates her deadlines.

chapters.title: Flour on the Ferry Glass
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Opening on the last week before the seasonal ferry pause, Ada delivers pastries to Sandoval Books and exchanges her usual three careful sentences with Emrys and his daughter Wren. Beat: longing disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Man Who Reads Spines
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. He catalogues his quiet obsession with Ada through the books he sets aside for her, while dodging Wren's blunt questions about why they never invite the baker to dinner. Beat: tenderness behind self-protection.

chapters.title: Theo Comes Ashore
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Theo Marchetti arrives with renderings for the Harborline development that would swallow her block, all charm and old familiarity. A loaded glance reveals they share a past no one on the island knows. Beat: dread wearing a smile.

chapters.title: Best Mistake of Our Twenties
chapters.summary: Alternating flashbacks in Ada's voice. Ten years ago in Copenhagen, Ada and Theo were rising chefs and lovers until his betrayal cost her everything. She never told anyone why she fled to the island. Beat: memory as wound.

chapters.title: Wren's Wish List
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Wren schemes to get Ada to bake her birthday cake, forcing Emrys and Ada into an afternoon of collaboration in the bakery kitchen. Something almost easy sparks between them. Beat: hope sneaking past defenses.

chapters.title: Council Chambers, Closed Doors
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The town council, led by the indebted Mayor Pruitt, fast-tracks Harborline. Theo privately offers Ada a payout and a job in exchange for her silence about their history. Beat: power showing its teeth.

chapters.title: First Flakes
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Weather warnings mount; Emrys invites Ada to the shop's evening reading as a friend, and she almost says yes before Theo intercepts her outside the bakery. Beat: the triangle tightening.

chapters.title: Stranded
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The storm hits early. Ada, fleeing Theo mid-argument, takes refuge in Sandoval Books just as the roads close—with Theo arriving minutes later, soaked and furious. Emrys locks the doors on a white world. Beat: trap sprung.

chapters.title: One Night, Three Histories
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Candlelight and cheap wine loosen tongues. Wren sleeps upstairs; Theo needles Ada with half-truths; Emrys watches the two of them and realizes he understands nothing about the woman next door. Beat: jealousy and confusion.

chapters.title: What the Storm Confesses
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Alone in the stacks after midnight, Ada tells Emrys the truth about Copenhagen—her disgrace, Theo's theft of her recipes and her name. He listens without flinching. Beat: being seen for the first time.

chapters.title: Morning After the Whiteout
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They wake having fallen asleep talking, hands almost touching. Theo, humiliated, leaves first and makes a call on the frozen porch. The thaw begins, but something between Ada and Emrys has permanently shifted. Beat: fragile new warmth.

chapters.title: Rumors and Rising Dough
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Island gossip does its work. Emrys, burned by his late wife's secrets, pulls back just as Ada leans in, and Wren notices the frost returning. Beat: fear sabotaging joy.

chapters.title: The Copenhagen Letter
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her old mentor writes: a head chef post awaits her in Copenhagen, contingent on leaving within the month. The career that could redeem her past sits on the counter beside the flour. Beat: temptation with a return address.

chapters.title: Harborline Advances
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo's permits clear suspiciously fast; the bakery's lease is suddenly 'under review.' Ada discovers Pruitt's campaign debts and suspects forgery but can't prove it. Beat: stakes made concrete.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. In the shop's back room, Ada and Emrys finally kiss—then she confesses she may leave for Copenhagen, and he retreats into old grief, telling her everyone he loves leaves. Beat: the wound reopened at the worst moment.

chapters.title: Wren Runs
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hurt and angry, Wren disappears during the harbor festival; Ada finds her in the bakery's proofing room and the two make a pact of honesty. Through Wren, Ada sees what staying could mean. Beat: love refracted through a child.

chapters.title: The Forged Signature
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Sorting Theo's old festival paperwork, Ada finds the smoking gun: Theo forged the landlord's signature on the option agreement years ago. She photographs it as the council vote is scheduled for ferry day. Beat: weapon found, conscience tested.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Waterfront
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo offers Ada everything—Copenhagen, redemption, silence kept—in exchange for the photos. For one long scene she genuinely considers it. Beat: the dark night of ambition.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Climax. At the dock, ticket in hand, Ada sees Emrys and Wren seeing her leave. She steps off the gangway, goes straight to the council meeting, and exposes the forgery before the vote. Harborline dies; Theo departs on the ferry alone. Beat: choice made publicly.

chapters.title: What Stays
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Aftermath and apology. Emrys admits he punished Ada for ghosts not hers; she admits invisibility was her oldest armor. Wren draws them a picture of three chairs at one table. Beat: repair begun.

chapters.title: Salt & Crumb, Reopened
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Spring prep: the bakery expands into the corner unit saved from demolition, with a reading nook supplied by Sandoval Books. Ada declines Copenhagen by letter, keeping the island instead. Beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Three Chairs at One Table
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing chapter. First morning of the new season: cinnamon rolls, a customer named Wren who refuses to pay, and Emrys crossing the street at opening time without hesitation this once. Ada lets herself be fully seen. Beat: quiet, earned joy.
